title: Why I Keep Reaching for Laravel to Build ERP Systems
excerpt: After shipping pharmacy, retail and deployment-panel ERPs on Laravel, here's what keeps it as the default choice over a JS-framework-first stack.
author: Manoranjan Das
bodyHtml:
MTP Pharma ERP, MTP Deploy and MTPsuite.com are all Laravel under the hood. That's not inertia — every one of these products lives or dies on boring things: migrations that don't corrupt data, background jobs that actually retry, and an admin UI (Filament, in most of these) that I don't have to hand-roll.

The parts that matter for ERP

Batch-wise inventory with expiry tracking needs transactional integrity across several tables at once. Eloquent plus database transactions makes that straightforward to reason about, and migrations give me a reviewable history of every schema change a client's data has been through.

Filament as the escape hatch

For admin-heavy tools like MTP Deploy's 20 modules, Filament turns weeks of CRUD-screen work into days, freeing time for the actually hard parts — SSH orchestration, SSL renewal, deploy script safety.

None of this rules out a JS frontend where it earns its complexity. But for backend-heavy line-of-business software, Laravel keeps winning on how fast I can ship something a shop owner will trust with their inventory.
